title: Bridging and Compressing Feature and Semantic Spaces for Robust Graph Neural Networks: An Information Theory Perspective

problem.claim: Real-world graph data contains noise and redundancy that degrade GCN graph representations, while distribution differences between feature and semantic spaces impair model generalization.

gap.claim: Existing studies commonly ignore the distribution difference between feature and semantic spaces, and existing denoising algorithms use random dropping rather than replacing potential noise with local neighboring representations.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes DIB-RGCN, a robust GCN framework guided by a dual information bottleneck principle.
The paper analyzes the causes of distribution differences and theoretically proves that minimal sufficient representations in specific spaces cannot guarantee optimal downstream-task performance.

The framework uses dual channels to regularize feature and semantic spaces, replaces potential noisy features and edges with local neighboring representations, and maximizes task-relevant information sharing between the spaces.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe DIB-RGCN as novel and characterize the replacement of potential noisy features and edges with local neighboring representations as innovative relative to random-dropping denoising algorithms.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly demonstrate the robustness of DIB-RGCN.
DIB-RGCN reportedly outperforms state-of-the-art methods on classification tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: GCNs aggregate information from higher-order neighbors and are important in graph learning.
Noise, redundancy, and feature-semantic distribution differences degrade representation quality and generalization.
DIB-RGCN applies a dual information bottleneck principle to seek robust graph representations.
The method combines theoretical analysis, dual-channel regularization, local-neighbor replacement of potential noise, and increased sharing of task-relevant information.
Experiments on real-world datasets report robustness and performance advantages on classification tasks.

source_observation.claim: The method regularizes feature and semantic spaces separately while maximizing their task-relevant information sharing.

interpretation.claim: Separating task-irrelevant information while preserving task-relevant cross-space information may improve robustness to representation mismatch.

application.claim: For models combining heterogeneous representation spaces, consider dual-space regularization with explicit control of shared information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the reported graph classification setting.

source_observation.claim: Potential noisy features and edges are replaced with local neighboring representations instead of being randomly dropped.

interpretation.claim: Structure-preserving local replacement may reduce noise interference while retaining graph connectivity information.

application.claim: When denoising structured data, consider local representation replacement when random removal would discard useful structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when local replacement is preferable to random dropping or how its effects vary across graph structures.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset identities, sizes, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or computational costs.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
